title: Real-space Floquet topology written by the orbital angular momentum of light
abstract: Floquet engineering usually treats light as a uniform control field that changes the topology of an entire driven material. Here we show that structured light carrying orbital angular momentum (OAM) enables a different regime, in which topology is written directly in real space. For ultrathin topological insulator films, circularly polarized Laguerre--Gaussian beams generate a radial Floquet mass whose sign changes define a topological annulus bounded by two concentric chiral ring modes. The transition is helicity selective: below a thickness-dependent critical frequency, left-circularly polarized light drives mass inversion, whereas right-circularly polarized light increases the gap and leaves the film trivial. Independently, the OAM quantum number shifts and reshapes the annulus without changing the frequency, intensity, or helicity. In the decoupled-surfaces limit, the same mechanism produces a purely Floquet-induced topological mass and a vortex-core zero mode. These results identify photon OAM as a control parameter for nonequilibrium topology and provide a route to programmable topological landscapes in quantum materials.
summary: This paper demonstrates that using structured light with Orbital Angular Momentum (OAM) allows for the direct, real-space writing of topological features in quantum materials like topological insulators. The topology forms a controllable annulus whose existence and geometry are independently tuned by the light's OAM number and helicity. This establishes OAM as a powerful control parameter for programmable topological landscapes.
main_problem: To demonstrate that structured light carrying Orbital Angular Momentum (OAM) can write topological properties directly into real space within a material, moving beyond global control mechanisms.
main_result: The study shows that OAM enables the formation of a topological annulus in ultrathin topological insulators, with the topology being controllable by the light's helicity and OAM number.
method: The analysis uses the leading Floquet–Magnus term to derive an effective Hamiltonian for a Dirac system driven by a circularly polarized Laguerre–Gaussian beam.
model_or_system: The system is modeled using quasi-two-dimensional Dirac systems realized in ultrathin Bi2Se3 films, driven by a time- and space-dependent optical field characterized by OAM ($\ell$) and circular polarization ($\hat{\epsilon}$).
key_observables: Topological annulus (defined by two concentric chiral ring modes), radial Floquet mass sign changes, and vortex-core zero modes.
important_parameters: Orbital Angular Momentum quantum number ($\ell$), light helicity ($\hat{\epsilon}$), and the ratio of peak optical amplitude to critical amplitude ($A_{	ext{peak}}/A_c$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the off-resonant regime approximation ($\omega \gg \Delta_0$) and the use of the leading Floquet–Magnus term.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the formation and expansion of the topological annulus for different OAM values ($\ell$), show the dependence of the inner and outer ring radii on the driving field strength, and summarize the helicity-selective crossover frequencies.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the theoretical framework using the Floquet-Magnus expansion, analyzes the role of helicity in driving mass inversion versus gap opening, and then demonstrates how OAM independently controls the geometry of the resulting topological annulus.
why_interesting: This work provides a concrete, optically controllable mechanism for engineering non-equilibrium topology in condensed matter systems, which is highly relevant for understanding light-matter interactions in topological materials.
